verdicts.task1_chapter_vs_code: Mostly true, one sentence false, several clarifications. FALSE as written: section 1 'A kosh grows each time you add to it' - grows only when full (cmp r9,r10; jb .space, src/sutram_compiler.asm:22490-22497; newcap = cap*2, :22500-22510). TRUE: slice-before-growth rule and reason (elements move; E_KOSH_VIBHAG / E_VIBHAG_ANKA at their emission sites; 'every way' true of the compiler but the chapter shows 3 ways, not the FFI/indirect-call shapes); block/kosh distinction (nirmmita given back, kosh keeps its bytes, cannot leave - E_KOSH_MANDAPA exists, 7 occurrences; mechanism correction: the kosh's storage persists, what ends is its liveness; a read-only pass to a non-keeping prakriya IS allowed); parimana() numbers 1008/0/0/96 all derive exactly (96 = 32 header + capacity 8x8; counts CAPACITY not length, not stated in the chapter); OOM message quoted exactly (src/sutram_compiler.asm:708) and the kosh IS unchanged (check runs before copy/descriptor update); the four absences in section 7 all true; 'a block field that is full' is a real third refusal (kshetra purnam, :728) but 'field' is never defined; E_PARIMITA message format exact, 'pankti 2' is the mandapa's line not the allocation's (line 5), runtime refusal after printing 512, exit 1, budget covers nirmmita inside the block only; nirmmita zeroing true (scratch zeroed at every allocation, including re-entry); all three mandapa exit paths rewind; mala fixed-size true; mala out-of-bounds READ checked true. Counts: mandapa 13/13, parimana 10/10, descriptor 0/0, slice 19 English (whole book); Sanskrit slice count 13 matches no rule tried (see brief_corrections). Sanskrit chapter is the SAME chapter, not shortened - same 7 sections, same programs, same numbers, same codes; nothing material missing.
verdicts.task2_beginner: No, not from this chapter alone - it uses vitti, chakra...tak, prakriya, nivartanam, likha, kosh_kship, kosh_gan, pankti_gan without explaining them, and never says how to run a program. With chapters 2-8 first, it is enough for block, budget and kosh, with four gaps: (1) the chapter's own numbers are not derivable - nothing teaches the kosh growth policy or that parimana() counts capacity, so the final example's 96 is a magic number (5x8+32=72, not 96); (2) the budget does not count the kosh, and the combined example puts kosh_kship inside a budgeted block without saying so; (3) 'a block field that is full' is undefined; (4) the OOM message cannot be seen happening (--fail-alloc exists for testing but is not documented for readers). Essential missing piece: the kosh growth policy and what parimana() counts for a kosh.
